plan: In a sealed-bid second-price auction with independent private values, the weakly dominant strategy is to bid your true value. This guarantees you win exactly when the second-highest bid is ≤ your value and pay that second price, maximizing expected profit regardless of others’ strategies. With no informative history and values i.i.d. U[0,49], deviating (over/underbidding) cannot improve payoff and can cause negative outcomes (overpay or missed profitable win). Therefore, bid exactly my value: 9.

In a sealed-bid second-price auction with independent private values, bidding your true value is a weakly dominant strategy. Overbidding risks winning when the second-highest bid exceeds your value, yielding negative profit. Underbidding risks losing when you would have earned positive profit (value minus second-highest bid). With one round and no informative history to exploit, the profit-maximizing choice is to bid exactly my value of $20.00.

[ This is a sealed-bid second-price auction. The dominant strategy is to bid your true value: overbidding risks winning at a price above value (negative profit), underbidding risks losing when winning would be profitable. There’s only one round, so no learning advantage. Values are independent and uniform; tie probability is negligible with 0.1 increments. Therefore, bid exactly my value: 20.0. ]
